A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same transformer OOD-learning theory and GROD algorithm. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison; renumbered and relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: v4 reports original Gaussian-mixture experiments, image and text evaluations, computational-cost measurements, ablations and visualizations.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments and adds evaluated baselines and ResNet50 results in Tables 9–10.

M1.justification: GROD retains its PCA/LDA boundary sampling, synthetic outliers, Mahalanobis filtering, soft labels, combined loss and adjusted-logit VIM inference. The shortened Section 6 retains its technical content in Appendix E; testing ResNet50 does not introduce an algorithmic modification.

E1.justification: The Gaussian-mixture, image, text and auxiliary outlier datasets and task requirements remain unchanged. ResNet50 uses existing image benchmarks. Texture and Places365 are newly discussed as excluded datasets, with no reported evaluation in either version.

E2.justification: v5 adds evaluated ATOM, POEM and DivOE comparators to all three existing ViT image comparisons in Tables 2 and 4–6, substantially expanding the outlier-exposure comparison beyond OE and MIXOE. The NLP comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Tables 9–10 introduce evaluations using ImageNet-1K-pretrained ResNet50 on the retained CIFAR tasks. Existing transformer training settings, validation-based checkpoint selection and evaluation metrics remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish reruns or revised protocols for those retained experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix H.3 adds an architectural-applicability check using ResNet50 outside the transformer-specific theoretical guarantees. Figure 1 stops displaying the gamma = 1 toy-ablation outcomes, although Section 5 still mentions that setting. The existing module ablations, other sensitivity studies and feature/likelihood analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Section 7 newly states that every experiment is repeated five times with different random seeds; v4 explicitly specified five seeds only for Figure 1. The revised Figure 1 also identifies its curves and bands as means and standard deviations. These are reporting additions, not evidence that run counts increased.

E6.justification: v5 adds results for three baselines across the existing vision comparisons and two complete ResNet50 comparison tables, while retaining the existing transformer table values. The new CNN findings are mixed: Table 10 reports GROD ID accuracy of 82.39 versus NPOS's 76.80, but mean AUROC of 88.51 versus 89.86. These are new configuration results, not improvements over v4 under identical settings. Figure 1 also removes the gamma = 1 result points.

T1.justification: v5 removes v4's FCNN-containment lemma, numbered 4.1/B.1, its constructive proof and its use in the sufficiency argument. The existing universal-approximation argument remains. The principal learnability theorem, probability definition and Jackson-type bounds otherwise retain their substance after renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: transformer OOD learnability conditions, capacity-dependent approximation bounds and theoretically motivated GROD with strong image/text performance. The abstract's added phrase 'under conditions' restates the already conditional framework.

C2.justification: Appendix H expands the discussion of overlapping ID/OOD distributions and explains why transferring the theory to CNNs requires separate approximation results. Additional passages explain VIM's complementary role and the exclusions of Texture/Places365, text OE comparisons and multi-GPU baseline timing. The new CNN results are interpreted as architectural versatility, although Table 10 does not support uniformly superior detection.

D1.justification: Appendix G.1 newly discloses that ATOM, POEM and DivOE require multi-GPU execution under the reported preprocessing, explaining their absence from runtime comparisons. Existing GROD hyperparameters, numerical implementation details, checkpoint-selection instructions and code-access information remain available.

R1.justification: Appendix A expands discussion of outlier exposure, POEM, auxiliary-input optimization and AUTO. New references include Jackson and CNN approximation work supporting Appendix H.3. The foundational positioning relative to Fang's learnability framework and the claimed transformer-specific contribution remain intact.

P1.justification: v5 adds introductory intuition for learnability and Jackson-type bounds, makes targeted prose edits, shortens Section 6 by removing detail retained in Appendix E, and moves Algorithm 1 into the appendix. Appendix H gains question-based subsections and a rewritten, relocated impact statement. Most prose and the main section sequence remain stable.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from two columns to one, substantially rearranging and resizing figures and tables. Tables 1–2 exchange numbering, vision tables gain comparator rows, and Tables 9–10 are added. Figure 1 changes its plotted range and adds a statistical legend; Figure 2 corrects the final training-stage heading to 'OOD Detection'.

improvement.justification: v5 offers broader comparisons, clearer statistical reporting and more explicit applicability discussion. However, its added empirical material contains consequential inconsistencies: ATOM's averages disagree between Tables 2 and 4, and Table 9 reports GROD mean AUROC as 97.72 although its three listed values average 97.39, reversing its ranking against NPOS's 97.58. Figure 1 also omits gamma = 1 despite the retained discussion. These problems undermine the added evidence, leaving the net quality benefit uncertain.
